_meta.indication: LOQTORZI is indicated, in combination with cisplatin and gemcitabine, for the first-line treatment of adults with metastatic or with recurrent, locally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC); and, as a single agent, for the treatment of adults with recurrent unresectable or metastatic NPC with disease progression on or after a platinum-containing chemotherapy.
_meta.receipt_date: August 31, 2021 (original BLA rolling submission final component); resubmission received June 23, 2022.

pivotal_trials.design: Adequate and well-controlled, multinational, double-blind, randomized placebo-controlled trial; patients randomized 1:1 to toripalimab 240 mg IV Q3W plus cisplatin and gemcitabine or placebo plus cisplatin and gemcitabine.
pivotal_trials.population: 289 adults with metastatic or recurrent, locally advanced NPC who had not received previous systemic chemotherapy for recurrent or metastatic disease.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was BIRC-assessed progression-free survival (PFS).
pivotal_trials.result: PFS HR 0.52 (95% CI 0.36, 0.74; p=0.0003), median PFS 11.7 vs 8.0 months; ORR 77% vs 66% (p=0.0353); final OS HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.45, 0.89; p=0.0083), median OS not reached vs 33.7 months.

pivotal_trials.design: Single-arm, open-label, multicenter, multicohort trial; patients received toripalimab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W as a single agent.
pivotal_trials.population: 172 patients with unresectable or metastatic NPC with disease progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy who received toripalimab 3 mg/kg Q2W as a single agent.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was IRC-evaluated objective response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1; the confirmed ORR and DOR were assessed by BIRC.
pivotal_trials.result: BIRC-assessed ORR 21% (95% CI 15, 28); median DOR 14.9 months (95% CI 10.3, NE).

key_safety: In JUPITER-02 (combination), most common adverse reactions (≥20%) included nausea (71%), vomiting (68%), decreased appetite (55%), hypothyroidism (38%); serious adverse reactions occurred in 43%. In POLARIS-02 (single agent), most common adverse reactions included hypothyroidism (27%), fatigue (22%), and cough (20%); serious adverse reactions occurred in 24% and fatal adverse reactions in 3.7%. Immune-related adverse events and infusion-related reactions were the significant identified safety issues.
target_moa: Toripalimab is an IgG4 monoclonal antibody directed against programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1); binding to PD-1 blocks its interaction with ligands PD-L1 and PD-L2, thereby maintaining the antitumor immune response.
modality: mAb (IgG4 monoclonal antibody, PD-1 blocking antibody)

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the biologic is not the first in its class, the trial design was acceptable, and the application did not raise significant safety, efficacy, or public health questions.

basis.text: Breakthrough Therapy Designation was granted (August 28, 2020) for the treatment of patients with recurrent or metastatic NPC, based on POLARIS-02.

requirement.text: 4471-1 Conduct a clinical trial enrolling a total sample size of 100 patients in the United States (U.S.) and Canada, that includes a sufficient representation of patients in racial and ethnic minority subgroups and is reflective of the U.S. population of patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), to further characterize the safety and efficacy of toripalimab in combination with cisplatin and gemcitabine in these patients. Include a sufficient number of patients with the keratinizing subtype reflecting the incidence of keratinizing NPC in the U.S. population. Conduct sparse sampling for supportive population pharmacokinetic and Exposure-Response (E-R) analyses. The E-R analyses may be used as supportive evidence for the efficacy and safety in the intended patient population. In the E-R analyses report, include an analysis of the presence and clinical impact of the neutralizing anti-drug antibodies on pharmacokinetics, efficacy and safety of toripalimab.

requirement.text: 4471-2 Conduct an assessment to determine the presence of neutralizing anti-drug antibodies against toripalimab in all patient samples that tested positive for binding anti-drug antibodies in all completed studies with unexpired immunogenicity samples, as well as all ongoing and planned studies by using a validated neutralizing anti-drug antibody assay. Evaluate the potential clinical impact of the neutralizing anti-drug antibodies on pharmacokinetics, efficacy and safety of toripalimab in a final report.
